This is the 0181 width number promoted from measured to proved: the finite, integer, level-1 form of the classical upper/lower sieve property, on the same phi_list machinery as the 0180 Legendre exact identity (no new axioms, no analysis, no RH claim).
claim: No RH claim: pure finite sieve combinatorics over exact nat/integer arithmetic, strict kernel replay on the pinned toolchain (no axioms anywhere in the file). The theorem level1_sandwich (x : NN) (ps : List NN) (hprime : every p in ps prime) (hdistinct : ps.Nodup) : L1 x ps <= (phi_list x ps : Z) AND (phi_list x ps : Z) <= U2 x ps, with L1 x ps = (x : Z) - sum_p (x : Z) / p (Nat-division cast, the floor form) and U2 x ps = L1 x ps + sum_{p<q} (x : Z) / (p q). Proof structure (all in-tree, all theorems): the band is proved pointwise through the prime-divisibility counting function mcount(ps, n) = #{p in ps | p | n}: (i) card_mulps (#{n in [1,x] | p | n} = x/p, the scaled-tail-set image lemma), (ii) mcount_single_sum (the floor sum = the per-n counting sum, product reindex + floor), (iii) offdiag_pointwise + mcount_offdiag_sum (m(n)(m(n)-1) = the off-diagonal card = the ordered-pair floor sum, via the (F x F) - diagonal decomposition + the distinct-coprime product-divisibility bridge p,q distinct primes: (p | n and q | n) iff p q | n), (iv) ordered_parts / ordered_parts_disjoint / ordered_eq_two_pair (the ordered distinct pairs split into the unordered half + its swap, disjoint, sum = 2 x the unordered sum via a sum_bij through Prod.swap), (v) the integer bridges x_ones_sum / mcount_single_sum_Z / mcount_offdiag_sum_Z, (vi) the pointwise residuals: slack_t(m) = 1_{m=0} - 1 + m >= 0 (vanishes exactly at m = 0, 1) gives phi = L1 + sum_n slack_t(m(n)) (level1_lower), and slack_s(m) = m(m-1) - 2m + 2 - 2*1_{m=0} >= 0 (vanishes exactly at m = 0, 1, 2; equals (m-1)(m-2) for m >= 1) gives 2*(U2 - phi) = sum_n slack_s(m(n)) (level1_upper, by_contra + positivity). The band endpoints may be negative (L1 < 0 for dense prime lists, exactly as 0181 measured: sum_{p<=z} 1/p > 1 from z >= 5) — the theorems are the Z-form statements and the negativity is a feature, not a defect.
